policy: Every citation was retrieved from PubMed metadata in this session. Nothing is cited from memory.
verification_level abstract_reviewed means the abstract was read. title_metadata_only means only the title and metadata were available, so no claim is drawn from it.
No numeric statistics, thresholds or prevalence figures from these sources appear in patient text.
Statements marked GENERAL_PENDING in recommendations have no retrieved citation and are queued for clinical review.
not_retrieved: WAO position papers and ACAAI practice parameters (other than the practice parameter title E23)
NICE guidance on food allergy and drug allergy
Assay manufacturer documentation (for example ImmunoCAP, ALEX2)
Full texts of all listed articles

evidence.title: EAACI guidelines on the diagnosis of IgE-mediated food allergy.
evidence.claims_supported: EAACI guideline: food allergy diagnosis starts with an allergy focused history, then tests of IgE sensitization. Serum specific IgE and skin prick tests are well supported for foods such as peanut and cashew, with poorer test performance for foods such as wheat and soya.
evidence.limitations: Abstract only. The full text was not read, and no numeric thresholds are taken from it.
evidence.retrieved_via: PubMed (NCBI) metadata and abstract retrieval in this session

evidence.title: Systematic review and meta-analyses on the accuracy of diagnostic tests for IgE-mediated food allergy.
evidence.claims_supported: Systematic review with meta-analyses of diagnostic test accuracy for IgE mediated food allergy (149 studies). Supports the principle that test accuracy varies by food and test, so a positive test alone is not a diagnosis.
evidence.limitations: Abstract only. Food by food accuracy figures are not reproduced in the KB.
evidence.retrieved_via: PubMed (NCBI) metadata and abstract retrieval in this session

evidence.title: EAACI Molecular Allergology User's Guide 2.0.
evidence.journal: Pediatric allergy and immunology : official publication of the European Society of Pediatric Allergy and Immunology
evidence.claims_supported: EAACI Molecular Allergology User's Guide 2.0: component resolved diagnosis helps identify the elicitors of IgE mediated allergy and supports interpretation of cross reactivity.
evidence.limitations: Abstract only. Individual component interpretations are not used in patient text.
evidence.retrieved_via: PubMed (NCBI) metadata and abstract retrieval in this session

evidence.title: EAACI guidelines on the management of IgE-mediated food allergy.
evidence.claims_supported: EAACI guideline on management of IgE mediated food allergy: after a confirmed diagnosis, allergen avoidance with dietary advice, a written treatment plan and education on recognising symptoms are essential.
evidence.limitations: Abstract only. Applies after confirmed diagnosis, so it does not support avoidance on IgE alone.
evidence.retrieved_via: PubMed (NCBI) metadata and abstract retrieval in this session

evidence.title: EAACI guidelines: Anaphylaxis (2021 update).
evidence.claims_supported: EAACI anaphylaxis guideline (2021): anaphylaxis is a clinical emergency. Prompt intramuscular adrenaline is first line management, and adrenaline auto injectors are recommended for patients in the community.
evidence.limitations: Abstract only. Emergency wording in the KB is deliberately kept general and non-prescriptive.
evidence.retrieved_via: PubMed (NCBI) metadata and abstract retrieval in this session

evidence.title: Controversies in drug allergy: In vitro testing.
evidence.journal: The Journal of allergy and clinical immunology
evidence.claims_supported: Review of in vitro testing in drug allergy: only a few in vitro tests are available for routine diagnosis, many are restricted to research laboratories, and tests have varying sensitivity and specificity.
evidence.limitations: Abstract only. Used to justify drug specific caution rules, not drug by drug validity claims.
evidence.retrieved_via: PubMed (NCBI) metadata and abstract retrieval in this session

evidence.title: Allergic reactions to antibiotics, mainly betalactams: facts and controversies.
evidence.journal: European annals of allergy and clinical immunology
evidence.claims_supported: Review of allergic reactions to antibiotics, mainly beta lactams: reactions are classed as immediate or non-immediate, immediate reactions may be IgE mediated, non-immediate rashes may involve T cells, and evaluation is complex and history led.
evidence.limitations: Published in 2005, so assay and practice details may be dated. Only broad principles are used.
evidence.retrieved_via: PubMed (NCBI) metadata and abstract retrieval in this session

evidence.title: Diagnosis and treatment of Hymenoptera venom allergy: S2k Guideline of the German Society of Allergology and Clinical Immunology (DGAKI) in collaboration with the Arbeitsgemeinschaft für Berufs- und Umweltdermatologie e.V. (ABD), the Medical Association of German Allergologists (AeDA), the German Society of Dermatology (DDG), the German Society of Oto-Rhino-Laryngology, Head and Neck Surgery (DGHNOKC), the German Society of Pediatrics and Adolescent Medicine (DGKJ), the Society for Pediatric Allergy and Environmental Medicine (GPA), German Respiratory Society (DGP), and the Austrian Society for Allergy and Immunology (ÖGAI).
evidence.claims_supported: German S2k guideline on Hymenoptera venom allergy: venom is injected by stings, some components are allergens, systemic reactions follow stings in about 3 percent of the general population over a lifetime, and large local reactions usually do not need specific diagnosis or immunotherapy.
evidence.limitations: German guideline. Applicability to Indian species and local practice has not been verified.
evidence.retrieved_via: PubMed (NCBI) metadata and abstract retrieval in this session

evidence.title: Shellfish and House Dust Mite Allergies: Is the Link Tropomyosin?
evidence.claims_supported: Shellfish tropomyosin is a pan-allergen also present in house dust mites and cockroaches. Tropomyosins from mites share high sequence homology with shellfish, and cross reactivity and correlated sensitization are described.
evidence.limitations: Review. Cross reactive sensitization does not prove clinical shellfish allergy.
evidence.retrieved_via: PubMed (NCBI) metadata and abstract retrieval in this session

evidence.title: IgE sensitization to house dust mite and cockroach allergens in asthmatic and allergic patients in the tropics.
evidence.claims_supported: Study in a tropical country (Colombia): cockroach sensitization was present in 29 to 40 percent of allergic and asthmatic patients, most were co-sensitized to house dust mite, and cockroach IgE levels were lower than mite IgE.
evidence.limitations: Colombian cohort. Indian prevalence is not claimed.
evidence.retrieved_via: PubMed (NCBI) metadata and abstract retrieval in this session

evidence.title: Cross-reactivity between aeroallergens and food allergens.
evidence.claims_supported: Review of cross reactivity between aeroallergens and foods. Describes birch-apple, cypress-peach, celery-mugwort-spice, mugwort-peach, mugwort-mustard, ragweed-melon-banana and goosefoot-melon associations, Alternaria-spinach, mite-shrimp, cat-pork and bird-egg syndromes.
evidence.limitations: Review. Describes the existence of associations, not their frequency in India. Birch is not in this catalogue.
evidence.retrieved_via: PubMed (NCBI) metadata and abstract retrieval in this session

evidence.title: Natural rubber latex allergy: causes, symptoms, and modern diagnostic methods.
evidence.claims_supported: Systematic review of natural rubber latex allergy: latex proteins (Hev b) are highly sensitising, healthcare workers and industrial workers are at increased risk, and reactions can be severe.
evidence.limitations: Abstract only. Prevalence figures are not used in patient text.
evidence.retrieved_via: PubMed (NCBI) metadata and abstract retrieval in this session

evidence.title: Revisiting Latex-Fruit Syndrome after 30 Years of Research: A Comprehensive Literature Review and Description of Two Cases.
evidence.claims_supported: Review of latex-fruit syndrome: cross reactivity between latex and fruit allergens, with banana, avocado, kiwifruit and papaya the most commonly implicated fruits. Prevalence in latex allergic patients varies widely (4 to 88 percent).
evidence.limitations: Wide variation in reported prevalence. No percentage is used in patient text.
evidence.retrieved_via: PubMed (NCBI) metadata and abstract retrieval in this session

evidence.title: Anisakiasis: A Decade of Molecular and Diagnostic Advancements (2015-2026).
evidence.claims_supported: Review of anisakiasis molecular and diagnostic advances: Ani s 7 remains the gold standard serological marker, and alpha-Gal epitopes in larvae suggest a possible link to alpha-gal syndrome.
evidence.limitations: Review. The alpha-Gal link is described as a suggestion only.
evidence.retrieved_via: PubMed (NCBI) metadata and abstract retrieval in this session

evidence.title: Allergic Anisakiasis: An Integrated Review of Human, Animal and Cellular Evidence.
evidence.claims_supported: Review of allergic anisakiasis: caused by eating fish contaminated with Anisakis larvae, with risk linked to raw or undercooked seafood, IgE mediated and gastro-allergic forms, and allergenic proteins that persist despite standard food processing.
evidence.limitations: Abstract only. Cooking advice in the KB is limited to lowering infection risk.
evidence.retrieved_via: PubMed (NCBI) metadata and abstract retrieval in this session

evidence.title: Update on occupational contact urticaria: a systematic narrative review.
evidence.journal: Current opinion in allergy and clinical immunology
evidence.claims_supported: Narrative review of occupational contact urticaria: immediate type reactions can be irritant or IgE mediated, may include generalised urticaria and anaphylaxis, and causative agents include natural rubber latex and cosmetic ingredients such as henna.
evidence.limitations: Abstract only. Contact urticaria differs from contact dermatitis, which is not IgE mediated.
evidence.retrieved_via: PubMed (NCBI) metadata and abstract retrieval in this session

evidence.title: Alpha-gal allergy in a South Asian country.
evidence.claims_supported: Report of alpha-gal syndrome from the Indian subcontinent (57 patients, 2018 to 2024): delayed allergy to red meat with symptoms up to 8 hours after eating, sensitization via tick bites, and some patients with allergy to bovine containing vaccines.
evidence.limitations: Single centre series in a South Asian country.
evidence.retrieved_via: PubMed (NCBI) metadata and abstract retrieval in this session

evidence.title: Reported food-related symptoms and food allergen sensitization in a selected adult population in Hyderabad, India: A hospital-based survey.
evidence.journal: The journal of allergy and clinical immunology. Global
evidence.claims_supported: Hospital based survey of 1622 adults with atopic disease in Hyderabad, India: foods reported as triggers and tested by skin prick and specific IgE included chickpea, cabbage, eggplant, walnut and cumin. Most patients had a total IgE above 144 kU/L.
evidence.limitations: Selected hospital population with atopic disease. Not representative of the general population.
evidence.retrieved_via: PubMed (NCBI) metadata and abstract retrieval in this session

evidence.title: House dust mite reduction and avoidance measures for treating eczema.
evidence.journal: The Cochrane database of systematic reviews
evidence.claims_supported: Cochrane review of house dust mite reduction and avoidance measures for eczema. Supports caution about promising benefits from avoidance measures.
evidence.limitations: Eczema population only. Avoidance advice for rhinitis or asthma is marked as general and pending review.
evidence.retrieved_via: PubMed (NCBI) metadata and abstract retrieval in this session

evidence.title: Patch-test reactions to topical anesthetics: retrospective analysis of cross-sectional data, 2001 to 2004.
evidence.claims_supported: North American Contact Dermatitis Group patch test data (10,061 patients, 2001 to 2004): 3.4 percent had an allergic patch test reaction to at least one topical anaesthetic. Supports patch testing as the relevant route for contact allergy to topical anaesthetics.
evidence.limitations: North American data from 2001 to 2004.
evidence.retrieved_via: PubMed (NCBI) metadata and abstract retrieval in this session

evidence.title: Occupational anaphylaxis: A Position Paper of the German Society of Allergology and Clinical Immunology (DGAKI).
evidence.claims_supported: German position paper on occupational anaphylaxis: Hymenoptera venoms, food and drugs are the most common triggers, and a detailed history is required. Few commercially available quality tested allergens exist for both skin and IgE testing.
evidence.limitations: German position paper.

evidence.title: Behind the scene: Paracetamol hypersensitivity in children.
evidence.journal: Pediatric allergy and immunology : official publication of the European Society of Pediatric Allergy and Immunology
evidence.claims_supported: Study of 60 children with suspected paracetamol hypersensitivity: diagnoses were confirmed by skin tests and oral challenge, supporting that suspected pain reliever reactions need specialist evaluation.
evidence.limitations: Paediatric study. Applied only as a general principle for adults.
